title: BLEND: Balancing Personalization vs. Generalization in Federated Vision–Language Models
claim: A federated system shares global adapters but keeps a personalized projection branch, with dual losses blending personalization and generalization.
layout: 2 regions: client-server diagram left, dual-stream model right; left-to-right flow
description: The figure has two parts divided by a dashed line. On the left, a cloud server connects through double-headed arrows to a column of stacked client servers labeled Client 1, 2, n, N-1 and N. Small icons mark the exchanged parameters as aggregatable. A curly brace links client n to a detailed model on the right. The model has a legend bar at the top. Two horizontal streams run left to right. The top stream takes a fox image through image patches into frozen pink vision transformer layers. The bottom stream takes the text 'An image of a [fox]' through text tokens into frozen blue text transformer layers. Hourglass-shaped adapters are added residually at each layer. A personalized projection adapter appears at the end of the vision stream. Both streams feed lime-green fusion and anchor score boxes, which lead to cloud-shaped losses and a final gold loss. Red dotted arrows point to the token callouts.
caption: Left: A FedVLM system with $N$ clients and a central server. Right: Schematic of the model introduced by {BLEND} for each client $n$, encompassing (i) a set of trainable and aggregatable global vision and text adapters, which are residually added to the transformer layers (i.e., $\{\delta_{n,\ell}^{\mathsf{Vis}},\delta_{n, \ell}^{\mathsf{Txt}}\}_{\ell=1}^{L}$), (ii) a trainable personalized vision projection adapter, which is integrated in a new branch and kept local during the training (i.e., $\delta_{n}^{\mathsf{Proj}}$), and (iii) dual loss functions (i.e., $\mathcal{L}^{\mathsf{Fus}}_n$ and $\mathcal{L}^{\mathsf{Anch}}_n$), which are integrated into the final loss $\mathcal{L}_n$.
abstract: Federated vision-language models (FedVLMs) represent one of the emerging frontiers of machine learning, aiming to integrate federated learning within the fine-tuning pipelines of vision-language models (VLMs). In this work, we introduce BLEND, a new framework designed to jointly enhance the personalization and generalization capabilities of FedVLMs. BLEND proposes a selective VLM parameter fine-tuning and aggregation strategy that consists of (i) global vision and text adapters shared across clients, and (ii) a personalized vision projection adapter tailored to each client. BLEND further introduces a novel loss function that blends the outputs of the global and personalized adapters to achieve personalization, while simultaneously promoting generalization through a principled anchor design implemented via the projection heads of the zero-shot VLM. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BLEND consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, highlighting its ability to effectively balance personalization and generalization across diverse system settings. (Code is available at: https://github.com/payamsiabd/BLEND.git)
